def overlapping(seq1, seq2):
    """
    Check whether any value in sequence 1 exists in sequence 2.
    
    Args:
        seq1 (list): The first sequence.
        seq2 (list): The second sequence.
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if there is at least one common element, False otherwise.
    """
    # Using set intersection for efficiency and clarity
    return len(set(seq1) & set(seq2)) > 0

# Test cases based on your requirement
assert overlapping([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8, 9]) == False
print("Test passed: No overlap found.")

# Additional test case where they do overlap
assert overlapping([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [4, 5, 6, 7]) == True
print("Test passed: Overlap detected (elements 4 and 5).")

def overlapping(seq1, seq2):
    """
    Check whether any value in sequence 1 exists in sequence 2.
    
    Args:
        seq1 (list): The first sequence.
        seq2 (list): The second sequence.
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if there is at least one common element, False otherwise.
    """
    # Using set intersection for efficiency and clarity
    return len(set(seq1) & set(seq2)) > 0

# Test cases based on your requirement
assert overlapping([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8, 9]) == False
print("Test passed: No overlap found.")

# Additional test case where they do overlap
assert overlapping([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [4, 5, 6, 7]) == True
print("Test passed: Overlap detected (elements 4 and 5).")
